items.title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026: Day 2
items.summary: Day 2 at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, full of all themes across AI, investor-only session, more roundtables, and more. Register to save 50% on your pass.

items.title: NTangible bets it can predict how athletes will perform under pressure
items.summary: NTangible is building an analytics platform for collegiate sports organizations and other clubs to measure an athlete's "clutch" factor.

items.title: Scimplify raises $25M to challenge China’s grip on critical materials with AI
items.summary: Scimplify's annualized revenue run rate has tripled to $200 million as it eyes U.S. expansion.

items.title: Justice Department says North Koreans have infiltrated dozens of US companies
items.summary: U.S. authorities warn that sanctioned hackers are increasingly targeting Americans to act as facilitators between breached U.S. companies and Pyongyang.

items.title: Science Corporation implants its vision-restoring chip in its first Stargardt disease patient
items.summary: Max Hodak, the former president and co-founder of Neuralink, detailed onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt how his company's work with PRIMA is part of its path toward a novel brain-computer interface (BCI).

items.title: Cerebras CEO says we’re nearing a future where everyone has a personal AI assistant at home
items.summary: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman predicts a future where personal AI assistants become as commonplace as household appliances, running partly on local devices and partly in the cloud.

items.title: Industrial Next wants factory robots to switch tasks in minutes, not weeks
items.summary: Industrial Next helps manufacturers automate complex, delicate tasks that have traditionally required human labor.

items.title: Cerebras CEO pushes back on AI doomsday warnings
items.summary: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman has a message for AI leaders spreading doomsday warnings: Maybe stop talking? At TechCrunch Disrupt, he argued that the industry's focus on AI's risks is drowning out its p...

items.title: Helix Carbon says it can make iron cheaper by recycling blast furnace pollution
items.summary: The steel industry is a big polluter, but Helix Carbon can upcycle pollution from blast furnaces to drive down emissions and improve margins.

items.title: FBI arrests OpenAI employee accused of planting hidden recording device in conference room
items.summary: It's not clear exactly for what purpose the recording device was used, but FBI director Kash Patel said the scheme was to "capture sensitive communications about the company’s super intelligence techn...

items.title: Judge orders OpenAI to turn over hiring records in Apple trade secrets case
items.summary: A federal judge ruled that Apple can access OpenAI's interview materials involving former Apple employees, as well as private messages and testimony from key figures in the case.

items.title: Cambridge Heavy Industries has been quietly building a desktop fusion device
items.summary: Fusion power startup Cambridge Heavy Industries is building a small, laser-powered fusion device to fuel the coming wave of fusion power plants.

items.title: Licube wants to be the fuel provider to the fusion power industry — see how at TechCrunch Disrupt
items.summary: Fusion power plants will need a lot of lithium, and Licube is preparing to be a key supplier.

items.title: Niobia takes the guesswork out of some of tech’s most expensive mistakes
items.summary: The San Francisco startup aims to help battery and chip manufacturers identify defects on production lines, reducing downtime and costly mistakes.

items.title: Rivian’s startup Mind Robotics hires former Ford EV chief Doug Field
items.summary: Field also worked on Apple's secretive car project and oversaw development of the Tesla Model 3.

items.title: Flox Intelligence is building AI to keep wildlife away from trains, airports, and roads
items.summary: Flox's edge devices can identify animals and use species-specific sounds to drive them away from critical infrastructure.

items.title: Facebook is giving users more control over their algorithm
items.summary: Meta announced the launch of its new AI-powered feature, “Your Algorithm,” a feature it first launched on Instagram.

items.title: Forget rockets — Longshot wants to fire cargo into space from a gun. See it at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
items.summary: Longshot is trying to build a gun big enough to make space data centers a reality.

items.title: Laplace Intelligence red-teams robots and self-driving cars before they hit the real world
items.summary: University of Michigan spinout Laplace Intelligence uses AI agents and interactive simulation to stress-test robots and self-driving vehicles before deployment. The profitable startup is competing in...

items.title: Pluto Security raises $42M as AI gives enterprise security teams a new headache
